name: Internationalism
summary: Internationalism favours political and economic cooperation among states and peoples, and opposes ultranationalism and isolationism. In its liberal form it relies on multilateral institutions, international law, open trade and cooperation on shared problems; in its socialist form it stresses solidarity of working people across borders. Most adherents want stronger global institutions that states join and control by treaty, not a world government.
scope: Mainstream liberal internationalism from Kant's Perpetual Peace and the Cobden-Bright free-trade tradition through Wilson's Fourteen Points, the League of Nations and the UN era, with the proletarian (Marx, Lenin, the Internationals) and anarchist strands noted where they diverge. Domestic economic, cultural and moral questions are mostly inferred and marked low confidence, because internationalism is a doctrine about relations between states and peoples.

keyFigures.name: Immanuel Kant
keyFigures.role: Author of Perpetual Peace, proposing a federation of free republican states.

keyFigures.name: Richard Cobden
keyFigures.role: Free-trade campaigner who argued commerce would bring peace.

keyFigures.name: Woodrow Wilson
keyFigures.role: US president whose Fourteen Points proposed a league of nations, giving the liberal strand its name Wilsonianism.

sources.title: Liberal internationalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Multilateralism, democracy promotion, liberal intervention, open markets, transnational cooperation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Internationalism says nothing on domestic health systems; mainstream liberal and social-democratic internationalists lean towards public provision, and global-health cooperation (WHO) is part of the doctrine.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: socialist and Labour-linked internationalists favour labour protection, but liberal internationalists have no fixed view on wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open markets and liberal economic systems, though it does not claim markets always beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Liberal internationalists favour open markets and are not committed to nationalisation, while the socialist strand would say yes, so the mainstream leans against.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Domestic tax rates are not an internationalist question and the liberal and socialist strands split.

unions-good.rationale: The socialist strand organised through international labour bodies and Labour-style internationalists were pro-union; liberal strand is silent, so a mild inference.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not a doctrine concern; liberal internationalists accept property rights but pooling sovereignty and international law can override them, so mild disagreement at most.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from interest in global rules and from cosmopolitan worries that large multinationals can impose terms on weaker states.

cut-welfare.rationale: Internationalists describe an obligation to help others through leadership and charity, which sits badly with cutting welfare, but the doctrine does not address domestic welfare directly.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the socialist strand would endorse this; liberal internationalists are indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to rights and rule of law; counter-terror cooperation is accepted but the doctrine is not about domestic surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the doctrine; international drug-control conventions are themselves a product of multilateralism, so adherents split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; liberal internationalists are divided between free-speech liberals and those who accept international human-rights limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Kant required republican constitutions with separated powers as a condition of peace, and liberal internationalists pair democracy with the rule of law.

state-harmful.rationale: Internationalism builds institutions among states, and liberal internationalism relies on states joining rules-based bodies, so it rejects the view that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun law is a domestic issue; the doctrine endorses international arms control but not specifically domestic limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wilson called for armaments to be reduced to the lowest point consistent with domestic safety, and Kant wanted standing armies abolished over time.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The doctrine is silent and liberal adherents split between rights-based and anti-trafficking views.

decide-locally.rationale: Internationalism moves authority upward to multilateral bodies; it is not hostile to local government but does not prioritise it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from liberal rights outlook and international human-rights norms; not a stated tenet.

traditional-family.rationale: Not a doctrine concern; liberal and socialist internationalists lean progressive, but the link is weak.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Liberal internationalism is tied to liberal rights norms and modern adherents generally support it, though it is not a stated tenet.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-rights orientation of modern adherents; the doctrine itself is silent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from the secular, rules-based liberal orientation; the doctrine does not address religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Socialist internationalism backs decolonisation and anti-imperialism, and cosmopolitan strands opposed slavery and apartheid, but domestic remedies are not specified.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Internationalism is opposed to ultranationalism and takes a cosmopolitan outlook, though many accept that patriotism and internationalism can coexist.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal internationalists favour incremental institution-building, socialists favour revolution, so the family is split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands treat migration as an act of world citizenship and Kant's hospitality right protects foreigners, but migration policy is not core.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Strengthening multilateral bodies such as the UN is the central mechanism of liberal internationalism, aimed at moving politics from anarchy towards common institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Cobden and Bright held that free trade would pacify the world, though the socialist strand rejects it, so the answer is agree rather than strongly.

nation-first.rationale: Internationalism is defined as favouring cooperation among states and as opposed to ultranationalism and isolationism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Liberal internationalism is linked to liberal interventionism in Bosnia, Kosovo and East Timor, though Kant's non-interference article and socialist anti-imperialism pull the other way.

open-borders.rationale: Strict cosmopolitans are sympathetic but moderate internationalists keep borders; adherents are genuinely split.

limit-growth.rationale: Internationalists seek cooperation on environmental problems but liberal internationalism favours open markets and growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Cooperation on transnational problems such as environmental issues is a named liberal internationalist goal, though 'drastic' is not stated.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources describe no stance on technology; Angell-style interdependence arguments are economic, not technological.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not addressed; IAEA-style cooperation is endorsed but adherents split on the energy question.

revolution-justified.rationale: Liberal internationalism works through institutions and law, while the socialist strand endorses revolution, so the mainstream leans no.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technocratic multilateralism sits in tension with the democratic stress of liberal internationalism; the doctrine does not settle it.

central-planning.rationale: The liberal mainstream supports open markets; only the socialist strand would be sympathetic.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist internationalists would agree and liberals are indifferent to ownership forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist taxation is outside the doctrine, though Cobden's free-trade circle was sympathetic to land reform.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not an internationalist issue, and strands split.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Cobden and Bright campaigned against the Corn Laws and Wilson's programme called for removing economic barriers, so protectionism is opposed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The liberal mainstream favours open markets over strategic state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property distribution is a domestic economic matter that none of the sources assign to internationalism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only the socialist strand's long-term aim; the mainstream liberal strand rejects it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Liberal internationalists favour international financial institutions and stable rules, not abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and at odds with the liberal market outlook.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kant's first definitive article requires a republican constitution with separated powers, and liberal internationalism promotes liberal democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kant's commentary allows that a constitutional monarchy can satisfy republican requirements, but modern internationalists are indifferent to the form.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal internationalism promotes liberal democracy and relies on democratic peace theory.

direct-votes.rationale: Kant favoured representative government, but modern adherents have no unified view on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Only the socialist strand would favour councils; the mainstream supports parliamentary democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Wilson endorsed self-determination of peoples, but internationalists also stress territorial integrity, so they split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands rest on the equal standing of all human beings, which is incompatible with natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Internationalists oppose war between states but liberals accept force for collective security and socialists accept revolutionary violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Internationalism is opposed to ultranationalism and Angell argued that war was unprofitable and outmoded.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the secular, rules-based character of liberal internationalism; not a stated tenet.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, rule-of-law orientation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Collective security and international courts are central, which treats defence and justice as public functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Wilson called for national armaments to be reduced to the lowest point consistent with safety, which opposes a contest for superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitan and liberal internationalist traditions reject ethnic definitions of belonging, though Wilsonian self-determination was applied to national groups.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The socialist strand affirms it and the liberal strand rejects it, so the family is split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Strands split; the doctrine does not address outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources on internationalism do not discuss indigenous peoples, and adherents split between rights-based and state-sovereignty views.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Socialist internationalism backs anti-imperialism, but reparations are not a stated tenet and liberal adherents split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Internationalism favours universal cooperation across all nations rather than blocs defined by shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Internationalists stress obligation to assist the world, which sits against a morality of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberal internationalism emphasises rights and human-rights norms over community duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental cooperation is endorsed for practical transnational reasons, with no stated view on intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy appears nowhere in the doctrine and adherents have no common line.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open markets and trade-based prosperity, so it rejects this.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The doctrine is silent on the pace of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: The doctrine is silent on bioethics and no source assigns it a position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to democratic and rule-bound government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is outside the doctrine; liberal rights arguments and counter-terror cooperation pull in opposite directions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Internationalism looks to new institutions to replace power politics, which is a progressive, forward-looking project.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Liberal internationalism is itself an ideological programme, yet practitioners often claim pragmatism, so no clear answer follows.

direct-action.rationale: Liberal internationalism works through treaties, institutions and elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a stated tenet, though anarchist internationalists would agree and institutional liberals would be indifferent.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Incompatible with a doctrine built on trade, institutions and interdependence.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Cobden-style interdependence rests on exchange and specialisation; only a utopian socialist strand would disagree.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The socialist strand endorses it and liberals do not.

production-for-use.rationale: The socialist strand endorses it and liberals do not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist internationalists say yes and liberal internationalists say no, so the family is split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Only the Leninist strand would agree; the mainstream rejects it.

collective-farming.rationale: Only the Soviet-era communist strand of proletarian internationalism pursued collectivisation, which the mainstream does not.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Socialists argue competition under capitalism causes imperialism and war, while liberals such as Cobden and Angell held that commerce brings peace; the family is split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Funding international institutions and aid presupposes legitimate taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights outlook of the mainstream strand.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands emphasise individual rights, but liberal internationalists also endorse national self-determination.

conscription.rationale: Wilson's arms-reduction aim and Kant's call to abolish standing armies point against it, though collective security can need forces.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Liberal internationalism relies on democratic institutions and not on exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred; the doctrine treats the state as a legal and political community.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social-democratic and socialist strands accept material conditions for freedom, whereas classical liberal strands reject them.

media-academia-power.rationale: A populist claim with no basis in internationalist doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rests on the equal moral standing of all humans.

organic-representation.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; liberal internationalism favours party democracy.

total-state.rationale: Opposed to the liberal rights and market orientation of the doctrine.

national-rebirth.rationale: National rebirth is an ultranationalist theme, which internationalism opposes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Kant's preliminary articles bar acquiring states and forcible interference, and Wilson's programme called for territorial integrity guarantees.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contradicts Kant's republican constitution and liberal internationalism's rule-of-law basis.

bound-labor.rationale: Cosmopolitanism was used against slavery, and bound labour contradicts equal standing.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Liberal internationalism relies on reason and universal norms.

universal-morality.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands assert universal moral standing for all humans, and Wilson and Kant appealed to a universal moral law.

single-common-good.rationale: Cosmopolitans appeal to a universal moral order, but liberal internationalism also accepts pluralism among states, so no clear answer.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wilson-style self-determination might support it, but the doctrine has no position and adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Migration and return rights are not discussed in the sources beyond general cosmopolitan sympathy for movement.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist cause on which internationalism takes no stated position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Socialist strands favour it and liberal strands are indifferent, so the family splits.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is a domestic issue that liberal internationalism does not address.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Kant opposed war debt specifically but the doctrine does not address fiscal stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Liberal internationalism pairs open markets with liberal democracy, but the linkage is not stated as a thesis.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberal internationalism relies on law and institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points endorsed autonomous development of peoples and a league guaranteeing the independence of large and small states, and socialist internationalists support self-determination too.

force-without-un.rationale: Liberal internationalism emphasises multilateral authorisation, though adherents split over cases like Kosovo.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kant stressed reason but modern adherents do not hold a position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Strict cosmopolitans deny that compatriot status should matter for need, though moderates allow special duties.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is a domestic matter outside the doctrine.

class-collaboration.rationale: The liberal strand favours cooperation and the socialist strand does not, so adherents split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist and radical rejection of heritage is foreign to the doctrine.

dominated-front.rationale: Internationalism favours inclusive cooperation, not blocs against particular powers, although the socialist anti-imperialist strand might agree.

workers-nation.rationale: The socialist internationalist strand holds that workers unite across borders, and the liberal strand is opposed to nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights orientation of mainstream adherents, since the doctrine does not address gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Open financial markets are part of liberal internationalism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cosmopolitan values were used against apartheid and slavery.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist strand agrees, liberal strand disagrees.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Cooperation on environmental issues is a named goal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands value cultural exchange and protect migrants' ties; assimilation demands are not part of the doctrine.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory contrary to the cosmopolitan treatment of migration as legitimate.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not addressed; the EU and UN models mix methods.

national-mission.rationale: Liberal internationalism promotes democracy cooperatively through institutions, and the article says treating all states equally is best, though Wilsonianism has a missionary reputation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources describe no stance on patriarchy, and strands differ in whether they adopt feminist analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: This populist claim contrasts with the institutional trust of liberal internationalism, though it is not addressed directly.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inconsistent with the equal moral standing of all persons.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The ICC and individual accountability for international crimes are cosmopolitan institutions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Internationalists want states to fund and join broad multilateral work on health, environment and development.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the universal moral standing of all humans.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism holds that every person has equal standing regardless of nationality or ethnicity, as the SEP describes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist internationalists, notably Trotskyists, say socialism needs world revolution, while liberal internationalists have no stake in the question.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Socialist anti-imperialist strand agrees, liberal strand mostly does not address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Domestic personal-law questions are outside the doctrine.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restricting conversion violates the liberal rights norms that liberal internationalism promotes, including freedom of religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A domestic religious-cultural law issue not addressed by the doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The doctrine does not address religious instruction in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Only a Leninist idea; the mainstream rejects it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kant's republican constitution and Wilsonian self-determination rest on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist goals contradict the Cobdenite free-trade tradition.

population-transfer.rationale: Kant bars forcible interference and the cosmopolitan right of hospitality protects foreigners.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kant bars aggression but liberal internationalists accept collective force, so adherents split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Internationalists emphasise cooperation and held that struggle between peoples is outdated, though they credit economic competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Liberal democracies split on this; not addressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Kant's republicanism is close to this idea, but modern adherents do not use the term, so it is not clearly answered.

separated-powers.rationale: Kant's republican constitution separates legislative and executive powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only the Leninist strand of proletarian internationalism endorses a vanguard party, which the mainstream does not.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Cosmopolitan justice strands emphasise needs of the global poor, but the principle is not stated for domestic law.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that the doctrine does not address.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The socialist and Labour traditions of internationalism defend strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cosmopolitan global-justice work blames institutions for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands value diversity and exchange.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in sources on internationalism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kant limited conduct even in war and liberal internationalists defend rule of law.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed; free-trade liberals would dislike them, socialists favour them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of the press violates the liberal rights norms that liberal internationalism promotes.

party-commands-army.rationale: Contradicts Kant's separation of powers and civilian republican control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Cosmopolitan strands are sympathetic to migrants, but naturalisation is not a doctrinal topic.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Only some socialist internationalists, in the Paris Commune tradition, would agree; liberals are indifferent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding discipline is a Leninist feature, while liberal internationalists are indifferent to party organisation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Internationalism favours multilateralism and limited supranational powers; the EU is the standard example of pooling sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Kant's separated powers and liberal democracy favour civilian parliamentary control.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance has no bearing on the doctrine.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clerics contradicts the liberal democratic orientation of liberal internationalism and Kant's republican constitution.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Zimmerwald socialists said yes, liberal internationalists strongly said no and supported the war effort or the League, so the family is split.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights outlook of the mainstream strand.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from republican constitution and separated powers.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not part of the doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours cooperative security and alliances such as NATO, which is an example of its interventions.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from the open-market orientation of the doctrine; the idea is a niche domestic proposal.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not a doctrine, but Wilson sought arms reductions and collective security.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; internationalism is urban-cosmopolitan by outlook.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Self-determination supports it but the doctrine also stresses peaceful settlement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: This populist idea runs against the expert and institutional orientation of internationalism, though it is not discussed directly.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cosmopolitan cultural strand values diversity and equal standing, though it is not a settled tenet.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from human-rights norms in international law; not a stated tenet.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from liberal outlook and multilateral health cooperation.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is a domestic moral issue outside the doctrine.

minority-language-support.rationale: Wilson's points call for autonomous development for peoples, which implies minority recognition.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and liberal adherents split between pluralist and uniform-law views.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's nonconformity argument is not part of internationalist sources, so no position is implied.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Global-justice strands favour relief, but liberal internationalists often favour orderly repayment.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist anti-imperialists agree and liberals do not.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; self-determination might favour it but nothing in the sources says so.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal internationalism pairs democracy with open markets.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Moderate and strict cosmopolitans accept a duty to aid foreigners in need, and the Wikipedia article says internationalists feel obliged to help the world through leadership and charity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Liberal internationalism treats arms control as a field for cooperation.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Kant's republican constitution does not specify how the executive is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from liberal economic orientation; not stated.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Wilson's programme favours impartial settlement of claims and peaceful agreements.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Liberal and socialist strands disagree about property, so the family is split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Trotskyist and left-communist internationalists say yes while Leninist and liberal strands say no, so the family splits.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental cooperation is a named goal; precaution is inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Cooperative security through institutions such as NATO is part of the liberal internationalist doctrine, and Wilson's Point XIV proposed mutual guarantees.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Wilson's points guarantee independence and territorial integrity, and Kant bars acquiring a state.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not addressed in the doctrine.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not specified; Kant required separation of powers but not a ceremonial head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Territorial integrity and self-determination pull in different directions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements are compatible with pooled sovereignty but no source links the two.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not a matter for the doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: The doctrine takes no view on the origins of character, though universal equal moral worth hints at environmentalism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kant's republican constitution requires law over force.

space-expansion.rationale: Outer space cooperation exists as a multilateral field, but the doctrine does not call it a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Kant favoured republic with separated powers but the doctrine is not about this classical formula.

leader-cult.rationale: Contradicts the republican and rule-of-law outlook.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the doctrine.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Only a Maoist theory; the mainstream and most socialist internationalists reject it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Socialist strand favours it; liberal strand does not.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan protection of individual rights and human-rights norms.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Kant's articles bar forcible interference and Wilson's programme called for guarantees of territorial integrity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy violates the liberal rights norms, including freedom of belief, promoted by liberal internationalism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes violate the individual rights norms that liberal internationalists promote.

common-currency.rationale: Pooling of sovereignty and economic integration; the euro is the main example.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Internationalism favours universal cooperation, not unions of kin peoples, though supranational unions are accepted.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Wilson's points call for autonomous development of peoples within states.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Internationalists favour equal rights for minorities everywhere, but a founded homeland is also compatible with self-determination, so adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist internationalists affirm historical materialism, while liberal internationalists such as Cobden and Murray stress ideas and moral law.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cobdenite free-trade tradition favours competition and open markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not addressed; international financial institutions have given rescue loans, but the doctrine takes no stated stand.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal internationalism relies on courts, international law and rule-based norms.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not part of the doctrine and adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs contradict free trade and interdependence.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Cooperation on environmental and labour issues is endorsed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral incentives are a Guevarist idea outside the mainstream doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Only the foco-theory revolutionary tradition holds this; the mainstream works through institutions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Kant's republican constitution is incompatible with hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cosmopolitan outlook contrasts with nation-centred education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Wilson called for colonial claims to give equal weight to the interests of the affected populations, and socialist internationalism opposed imperialism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Opposed to ultranationalism, though some adherents accept moderate patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: A US domestic policy debate that the doctrine does not address.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not addressed by internationalist sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Liberal internationalists say yes and Marxists say no, so the family is split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: Wilson's self-determination and colonial claims point against claims of special influence over former imperial regions, though liberal internationalists accept some post-imperial ties.

delink-world-market.rationale: Liberal internationalism backs open trade and integration, and Wilson's points call for removing economic barriers; the socialist strand also favours cooperation over delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Proletarian internationalism holds that workers everywhere share interests and liberal internationalism does not split workers by country, so adherents reject this; inferred from the solidarity strand.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: internationalists favour universal human-rights norms and law, which cut against a general right to discriminate, though classical liberals among them might differ.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal internationalism supports binding legal protection of rights, and Kant's republican constitutions rest on rule of law; a domestic entrenched bill is inferred from this.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Wilson's self-determination principle implies revisiting settlements imposed without the consent of peoples.

elective-rulers.rationale: Kant requires republican constitutions with representative rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism relies on majority and treaty rules, not unanimity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: liberal tradition accepts resistance against tyranny, though Kant denied a right of rebellion.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kant's republic rests on a representative legislature.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitan moral concern extends widely to sentient beings.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; mainstream humane-use view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitan duties of aid extend the duty to help the badly off.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: engagement is its rule; opposes isolationism, though this concerns personal life.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: not a theme in liberal internationalism, which sees media as a means of exchange.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: liberal and Marxist strands differ on this Gramscian claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Liberal internationalism holds open trade benefits all, against structural-extraction claims.

native-born-offices.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rejects privileging citizens by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: Liberals have no view on socialist parties; the proletarian strand split on Moscow direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open trade, aid and investment over self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Wilson's Point 8 backed returning Alsace-Lorraine but the doctrine generally opposes revanchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: equal individual rights, not group-based rank.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to ultranationalism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: liberal democracy promotion condemns both as unfree.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; mainstream historiography is rejected by cosmopolitans too.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: universalist equal concern for all groups.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: universalist equal protection for all victims.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal internationalism promotes democratic institutions as broadly universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Kant demands abolishing standing armies and civil control of arms.

filial-duty.rationale: Internationalism is a doctrine about relations between states and peoples and says nothing on family obligations; adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine bears on how officials are recruited; Kant favours republican representative government, but liberal and socialist strands differ on civil-service selection.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from liberal internationalism's commitment to open trade and investment and the Fourteen Points' removal of economic barriers; security carve-outs make it a mild rather than strong disagreement.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The doctrine is silent on family law, and liberal and socialist internationalists have no common line.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred as split: the proletarian and anarchist strands favour mandated, recallable delegates, while liberal internationalists accept ordinary representative democracy.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Domestic pension design is not addressed; liberal internationalists lean market-friendly and socialist ones favour state systems, so adherents are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: the liberal mainstream and Kant's republican order assume ordinary private property, though the proletarian and anarchist strands would favour common land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from Kant's requirement of republican constitutions and the Fourteen Points' stress on accountable, open government; budget control is not discussed directly.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from internationalism's opposition to ultranationalism and its support for self-determination and minority peoples; language policy itself is not addressed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to economic nationalism and its support for free movement of capital, goods and people; not addressed directly.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Domestic anti-discrimination doctrine is outside internationalism, and adherents are split between liberal intent-based and egalitarian outcome-based views.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; socialist internationalists criticise consumerism while liberal internationalists defend commerce as pacifying (Kant, Cobden).

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kant's sixth preliminary article bars states from interfering by force in another state's constitution and from fomenting treason, and liberal internationalism stresses sovereignty and multilateral law; proletarian internationalists would dissent for revolutionary movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Kant's fifth preliminary article forbids forcible interference in another state's constitution and government, and the Fourteen Points rest on self-determination, so unilateral bloc-enforcement runs against the doctrine.

corporate-influence.rationale: Liberal and socialist internationalists distrust concentrated private power in politics; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Open exchange between states and peoples is central, so restricting foreign funding conflicts with it; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; internationalists favour open migration rather than state natalism; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Cooperation and open exchange between peoples imply opposition to local residency limits; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; liberal internationalists lean to markets, the socialist strand to guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Kant’s Perpetual Peace argues republican states are peaceful, and liberal internationalism promotes democracy for peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; internationalists generally favour law and its institutions over a right to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: Kant bars interference in other states but liberal internationalism supports humanitarian intervention; the absolute claim is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; the proletarian strand and liberal strand differ.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism and the scapegoating of minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream liberal and socialist support for legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Wilson called for open covenants openly arrived at and Kant required publicity in international affairs.

local-production.rationale: Open trade and the removal of economic barriers are central to Wilson and Cobden-Bright liberal internationalism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Internationalism builds formal treaty institutions rather than small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Mainstream internationalism wants international law and courts to bind states.

religious-nation.rationale: The doctrine opposes ultranationalism and rests on a shared humanity, not a national religion; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points and Kant's federation of free states rest on equality among nations, not tribute to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitan and internationalist ethics favour sharing resources across borders over local retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Liberal internationalism accepts private property and markets; common ownership of the means of production is inferred to be rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours coexistence and engagement through institutions and trade rather than a campaign to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalists lean towards market-friendly delivery of public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Internationalism does not address the question; liberal internationalists typically do not hold that religion is an illusion (inferred).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open markets and trade as drivers of prosperity and peace.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalists lean towards reaching equality through law and reform within the existing system.

socialized-care.rationale: Internationalism does not address domestic care work; liberal strands favour family and private arrangements (inferred).

purge-loanwords.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism, and linguistic purism is a nationalist cause; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Kant and Wilson stress good faith in treaties and the rule of law, from which binding agreements with internal nations are inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Internationalism builds on cooperation among states and institutions, not on small property-holding communes (inferred).

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from internationalism's opposition to ultranationalism and its respect for minorities and self-determination.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open markets, and so sees capitalism with international rules as workable; a third way is inferred to be unneeded.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to ultranationalism and its self-determination principle: internationalists treat peoples' present wishes, not ancestral claims, as the basis for borders.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine never addresses it, but a committed internationalist rejects denial of a well-documented genocide that international law was later built to prevent.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's commitment to individual rights and international human-rights norms, which have moved against criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal internationalism promotes democracy and open societies, and Kant's republican constitutions require a free public, so suppressing opposition is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from liberal rights norms and religious freedom; the doctrine is silent, so the answer is a mild disagreement.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points call for colonial claims to be settled with the interests of the populations given equal weight with the colonial power's claims, which rejects governing colonies for the metropole.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Internationalism does not address Islamic jurisprudence; the liberal strand favours international law over religious duty while the anti-imperialist strand sympathises with resisting invasion, so adherents are split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalists prefer change through law and institutions and would not endorse forcible removal on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The socialist strand favours direct popular participation while the liberal strand relies on representative institutions, so adherents are split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Internationalism is about relations between states; the proletarian strand would agree and the liberal strand has no fixed view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's rights-based universalism, which has extended to gender identity in international human-rights practice.

assisted-dying.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on end-of-life care and adherents differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Internationalism is a cross-cutting doctrine held on both left and right, but its own strands (liberal and socialist) sit on different sides, so adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: The proletarian strand follows Marx on alienation while the liberal strand does not, so adherents are split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan universalism, which rejects treating any culture or religion as inherently incompatible with others.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kant's republican constitution rests on the consent of citizens, and liberal internationalism is secular in outlook, so authority from God is rejected, though not centrally.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: A domestic matter the doctrine does not address; liberal internationalists lean towards neutrality in the state and others towards freedom of dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights tradition, which favours access to courts for complainants; the doctrine does not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: liberal and social-democratic internationalists favour open markets alongside social protection and global welfare duties.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wilson's Fourteen Points call for reducing national armaments to the lowest point consistent with domestic safety, and collective security still rests on force; Kant's ban on standing armies is an ideal, so abolition is mostly rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Open trade is central, but the doctrine does not address uneven domestic development; adherents have no fixed view.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Liberal internationalism rests on multilateral alliances and collective security and opposes isolationism, though it also opposes rival power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from Kant's call for republican constitutions among cooperating states; the doctrine itself does not address hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Internationalism says nothing about credit unions; adherents split between liberal market and socialist strands.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Liberal internationalists back IMF-style institutions while the socialist strand opposes their conditions, so adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the republican and consent-based government internationalism favours; property qualifications are not discussed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The doctrine concerns relations between states, not gender or ecology; adherents hold no common view.

reification.rationale: Only the proletarian strand uses this Marxist idea; the liberal strand ignores it, so adherents are split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The socialist strand would agree and the liberal strand would not; the doctrine is silent on press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kant's republican constitution rests on law rather than arbitrary rule; inferred, as the doctrine does not address domestic legal form directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: Internationalism stresses cooperation among all peoples and cosmopolitanism gives every person equal moral standing, which rules out racial limits on political rights.

online-participation.rationale: The doctrine does not address online deliberation; adherents are split on it.

open-government-data.rationale: Wilson's first point demanded diplomacy conducted openly, from which a general preference for open government is inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to ultranationalism and its commitment to cooperation across peoples; the issue is not addressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to ultranationalism and its solidarity across peoples and faiths.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: internationalism is about relations between states; citizens' assemblies are a domestic democratic device, though cosmopolitan strands have promoted global deliberative forums, so adherents are not united.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: internationalism takes no position on religious doctrine; liberal and socialist strands lean secular but adherents do not agree on reforming religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan concern for global distributive justice and solidarity across borders.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the universal human-rights framework that cosmopolitan internationalism endorses.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism backs universal rights including freedom of belief, so state-imposed atheism conflicts with it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: collective security and international law presuppose enforcement and ordered states, not abolishing police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its preference for negotiated multilateral settlements that include all parties in governing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from its support for global institutions and aid as shared responsibility, over reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Kant's republican constitution calls for limits on rulers, so term limits are a modest inference.

vote-delegation.rationale: Internationalism is a doctrine about relations between states and says nothing on delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan emphasis on shared global problems that need collective action.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the universal equal moral worth of persons in cosmopolitanism.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan principle of equal standing for all persons.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Liberal and socialist internationalists favour cooperation across borders and are more open to extending rights to resident non-citizens; inferred, not stated in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Internationalism is a doctrine about relations between states and says nothing on housing policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open trade and the Wilson tradition accepts property rights; abolition is not addressed, and WIPO-style cooperation points the other way.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalist militarism, and Kant's essay and Wilson's points favour disarmament, so drilled national-service youth movements are inferred as rejected.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Wilson's arms reduction and the arms-control tradition of liberal internationalism point toward non-proliferation; inferred, not stated on basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Kant bans standing armies and liberal internationalists favour collective security, but alliances with bases are common in the multilateral order; adherents are split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Liberal internationalism relies on international law and human rights institutions, which include recognising genocide under the UN convention.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Internationalism does not address how income relates to property; liberal and socialist strands differ.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Kant and liberal internationalism accept defensive force and collective security under the UN Charter, so an absolute ban is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism and myths of national purity; it is inferred that it rejects an unbroken ancient-origins view of the nation.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism, and honouring the dead as national martyrs and saints belongs to nationalist cults.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Liberal internationalism rests on law, diplomacy and reason, not a cosmic contest of good and evil; inferred from Kant and Wilson.

culture-before-state.rationale: Internationalism pursues cooperation among states and peoples, with no priority on cultural renewal before state-building; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism and Wilson's points stress equal treatment and minority guarantees, so reserving the economy for a majority is rejected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Wilson's self-determination was qualified by existing states and international stability; merging regions for one people is not an internationalist goal; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The proletarian strand stresses cross-border worker solidarity and liberal internationalism backs the ILO; independence from the state is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The socialist strand would agree but the liberal strand does not address it, so adherents split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Domestic ownership is outside the doctrine; liberal and socialist strands differ.

second-chamber.rationale: Domestic institutional design is outside the doctrine.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred; neither liberal nor socialist internationalism favours community-owned production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Kant's federation of states is a cooperative model, but the statement is about domestic towns and their delegates.

family-wage.rationale: Domestic wage policy is outside the doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; global-health cooperation is welcome but approval speed is not a doctrinal matter.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

person-over-state.rationale: Cosmopolitanism and Kant's idea that people are ends in themselves support the primacy of the person, applied here by inference.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Domestic territorial arrangements are outside the doctrine.

gm-crops.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and adherents would not agree on an answer, so it is left neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism and stresses solidarity across lines of nation and race, so organising around racial group interests runs against it.

racial-pride.rationale: Cosmopolitans do not condemn ancestry pride, but do not promote it either.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace bans aggression and the Fourteen Points aim at security, but collective-security enforcement means not all internationalists limit force to national defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Wilson's points redrew borders along lines of nationality, but internationalists also reject ultranationalism and treat nations as civic communities; adherents split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's universal, common-citizenship outlook; separate religious electorates divide a polity along communal lines.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: internationalism stresses cooperation and mutual trust among states, so plot narratives sit badly with it.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: liberal and social-democratic internationalists lean towards broad access to education; the doctrine itself does not address tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from cooperation on shared global problems such as climate; the doctrine does not specify the instrument, though market pricing suits its liberal strand.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan duties that extend beyond the present and one's own country.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Internationalism says nothing on gender and values; adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wilson's fourth point says national armaments will be reduced to the lowest point consistent with domestic safety.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Wilson's first point calls for open covenants of peace openly arrived at, and Kant bars treaties with secret reservations.

capital-controls.rationale: Liberal internationalism favours open trade and investment; the socialist strand is more mixed, so this is an inference.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism favours state monopoly of force under international law and disarmament of private armies.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: most adherents back collective security that can require force, though the socialist strand supports refusing wars between states.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: the socialist strand stresses solidarity of workers across borders through unions, while the liberal strand is mostly silent.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Internationalism is a doctrine about relations between states and says little about domestic income support; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Internationalism does not address domestic borrowing limits, and adherents split between fiscal rules set by treaty and national discretion.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Internationalists favour reforming trade, finance and aid through multilateral institutions, and the socialist strand seeks fairer terms for poorer peoples.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Liberal internationalism works through existing states and treaty institutions and favours reform, not revolutionary dismantling of the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism favours open trade and shared rules among states, not a variety of separate economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: internationalists want cooperation on shared environmental problems, but the texts do not decide whether nature is priced as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Internationalism opposes ultranationalism and treats the nation as a political arrangement, not a sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A domestic fiscal question that internationalism does not address; adherents are split.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine concerns exploitation between states, not within one, though its socialist strand might accept the idea.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Cosmopolitan thought grounds universal rights and the duty to all people in a common humanity.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: Wilson's open diplomacy and cosmopolitan outlook favour a free, informed public, and adherents mostly back independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Internationalism says nothing on religious truth; cosmopolitan tolerance of faiths does not entail a shared underlying truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Liberal internationalism in the Cobden-Bright tradition favours free trade over farm protection, though socialist strands might accept supports.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Internationalists favour arms reduction and collective security, and the Fourteen Points call for national armaments to be reduced to the lowest point consistent with safety.

workers-own-party.rationale: Socialist internationalists want worker parties and liberal internationalists do not; the doctrine as a whole is split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Cosmopolitan and internationalist thought supports universal human rights across borders, which covers bodily integrity and bans on harmful practices.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Universal rights are core to cosmopolitan and liberal internationalist thought, and equal property rights for women follow from them.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Internationalism does not address language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Internationalists favour cross-border regulation and treaties on shared environmental problems over private-law liability alone.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the universalist and legal-rational outlook, which does not give hereditary or customary authorities a national lawmaking role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Internationalists back cooperation on global environmental problems, but liberal and socialist strands differ on trading it against individual liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rule-of-law and human-rights outlook, which prefers judicial discretion over fixed penalties.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the openness to migration and cultural exchange that internationalists favour, which does not favour requirements; adherents are not unanimous.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: socialist internationalists back strong unions and union security while liberal internationalists favour free labour markets, so adherents split.

voter-id.rationale: The doctrine concerns relations between states, and adherents split on voting rules by their domestic politics.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan commitment to equal respect for all persons regardless of creed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Kant's republican constitution and Wilson's call for self-determination, which treat free elections as the mark of legitimate government.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: liberal cosmopolitan internationalism leans permissive on private morals, though the doctrine does not address it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on open exchange of goods, people and ideas across borders and from UN-centred human rights norms.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is silent on welfare design, and adherents run from liberal to socialist.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the universalist human-rights commitment of liberal internationalism, including equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: socialist strands often say so while liberal strands do not, and the doctrine itself does not address it.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan view that humanity is one moral community, which rejects biological racial hierarchy.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: internationalists back UN bodies and conventions on women's equality, which the member states implement through national agencies.

missingStatements.text: Countries should settle disputes through international courts and arbitration rather than by force.
missingStatements.rationale: Hobson anticipated international courts and congresses for settling disputes, and the UN and ICC are the doctrine's institutional core.

missingStatements.text: Governments should negotiate treaties and agreements openly rather than in secret.
missingStatements.rationale: Wilson's first point called for open covenants of peace openly arrived at, and Kant barred peace treaties with secret reservations.
missingStatements.declined: Open covenants are a narrow diplomatic-procedure point that few ideologies would contest; not worth a permanent statement.

notes: The liberal and proletarian strands answer differently on trade, capitalism, class and revolution; zeros on those items reflect a genuine split. Many domestic items are not addressed by the doctrine, so confidence is low and the salience check may exclude the profile.
